t:
That 
    (a),  
effective as of the first day of the first pay period which began after June 30, 1948, each of the rates of basic compensation provided by sections 412 and 415 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 (U. S. C., 1946 edition, title 22, secs. 867 and 870) which do not exceed $10,000 is hereby increased by $330. 
    (b) 
No additional compensation shall be payable by reason of the enactment of this section for any period prior to the date of enactment of this Act in the case of any person who is not a Foreign Service officer, a Foreign Service Reserve officer, or a Foreign Service staff officer or employee on such date.
 
    (c) 
No person whose compensation is increased by this section shall be entitled to any overtime pay, or compensation for night and holiday work, as provided in sections 201, 301, and 302 of the Federal Employees Pay Act of 1945, as amended, based on the additional compensation provided by this section for any pay period ending prior to the date of enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only raises basic compensation rates for Foreign Service personnel and limits retroactive and overtime pay. It concerns federal employees' pay alone; no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision. There is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or consultation, so nothing here could tempt a participation reading beyond the mention of affected persons.
fable.s: each of the rates of basic compensation provided by sections 412 and 415 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 (U. S. C., 1946 edition, title 22, secs. 867 and 870) which do not exceed $10,000 is hereby increased by $330.

qwen_block.w: This section mandates a specific increase in the basic compensation rates for Foreign Service officers and employees. It is a purely administrative provision regarding federal employee salaries and does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or interactions with states, tribes, or the general public described in the text.
qwen_block.s: each of the rates of basic compensation provided by sections 412 and 415 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 ... is hereby increased by $330.

opus.w: This section raises Foreign Service pay rates by $330 and limits back pay and overtime that would otherwise flow from the raise. It involves no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The people affected are federal employees receiving pay, which is not participation in a federal decision.
opus.b: The tempting reading would be to treat this as a federal decision affecting employees, since it changes Foreign Service pay. That fails because the section only sets pay rates. No one outside the federal government is consulted, no comment period or hearing is required, no rulemaking is authorized, and no one is given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates a salary increase for federal employees (Foreign Service officers and staff). It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The definition of participation requires interaction with non-federal entities (states, public, experts, etc.), whereas this is an internal administrative adjustment of federal compensation.
qwen_chat.s: each of the rates of basic compensation provided by sections 412 and 415 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 ... is hereby increased by $330.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute affects "persons" (employees), it involves them. However, the definition explicitly excludes internal government matters and applications for benefits. This section is purely about adjusting the salary scales of federal employees. There is no consultation, hearing, advisory board, or right to sue granted to outsiders. The actors are the government (setting pay) and its employees (receiving pay).
